first.rationale: I intend to test a guarded onboarding simplification because onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and inherited evidence suggests that reducing friction improves durable early adoption. This should support sustainable qualified revenue without immediately sacrificing economics in a price war. I will verify the two most directly relevant archived records before committing, while monitoring downstream qualification and retention rather than optimizing completion alone.

final.rationale: Run a standard, segmented onboarding simplification experiment this week, prioritizing self-serve SMB accounts where the evidence applies. Shortened onboarding improved completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention; signup simplification also improved activation and qualified revenue, though its small retention decline warrants guardrails. Measure qualified revenue, activation, time-to-value, retention, and onboarding completion—not completion alone—and avoid extrapolating the signup result beyond SMB.
